name: Commercial VRP (Variable Recurring Payment) Consent Setup

phases.name: VRP Consent Request
phases.description: A PISP/merchant (PER-006) submits a VRP consent request to the bank's Open Banking API (SVC-017) specifying the consent parameters: maximum single payment amount, maximum monthly amount, payment category, and expiry date. The bank's authorisation server (SVC-100) validates the TPP's registration and PISP permissions, and creates a pending VRP consent record. The customer is redirected to the bank's consent portal.
entry_conditions: TPP holds a valid FCA PISP authorisation
TPP has a registered client_id from Dynamic Client Registration (JRN-010)
TPP presents a valid access token with vrp:consent scope
exit_conditions: VRP consent record created with status = pending_authorisation
Customer redirected to bank's VRP consent portal with consent_id

phases.name: Customer Authentication and Consent Authorisation
phases.description: The customer authenticates via SCA (biometric/OTP) through the bank's digital channels. The bank presents the VRP consent parameters in plain language: payee details, maximum amount per payment, maximum monthly aggregate, payment category, and expiry date. The customer explicitly confirms or rejects the VRP consent. Upon confirmation, the bank issues an authorisation code to the PISP and creates the active VRP consent record.
entry_conditions: VRP consent record in status = pending_authorisation
Customer has an active current account (PH-001 prerequisite)
exit_conditions: VRP consent record updated to status = active
PISP receives OAuth authorisation code exchanged for access token

phases.name: VRP Payment Execution
phases.description: The PISP submits a VRP payment instruction referencing the active consent. The bank validates the payment against the consent parameters (amount within limits, consent active and not expired). Fraud scoring is applied. If all checks pass, the payment is executed as a Faster Payment. Subsequent VRP payments in the same consent do not require per-payment SCA (the consent acts as the delegated SCA).
entry_conditions: VRP consent record in status = active
Consent not expired and not revoked
exit_conditions: VRP payment executed as Faster Payment

phases.name: Consent Lifecycle Management
phases.description: VRP consents are managed throughout their lifecycle: the customer may revoke a consent at any time via the bank's consent dashboard (SCA required); consents expire automatically on the expiry date; the PISP may also delete the consent. The bank must notify the customer on consent expiry. Revoked or expired consents reject future VRP payment instructions immediately.
entry_conditions: VRP consent record in status = active
Customer initiates revocation OR consent expiry date reached OR PISP deletes consent
exit_conditions: VRP consent record updated to status = revoked or expired
EVT-158 VrpConsentRevoked published (for customer-initiated revocation or PISP deletion)
Future VRP payment instructions against this consent rejected

happy_path.description: PISP submits consent request → customer authenticates and grants consent → consent becomes active → PISP submits VRP payment → bank validates and executes as FPS.

alternative_paths.name: Consent Parameter Breach — Payment Rejected
alternative_paths.description: PISP submits VRP payment exceeding the consented maximum single payment amount or monthly aggregate. Bank rejects with 422 and reason code. Consent remains active.

alternative_paths.name: Customer Revokes Consent
alternative_paths.description: Customer initiates consent revocation via the bank's consent dashboard. SCA completed. Consent status set to revoked. PISP notified via webhook callback.

exception_paths.name: Fraud Score Threshold Exceeded — VRP Payment Blocked
exception_paths.description: Fraud Detection (SVC-013) scores the VRP payment above the fraud threshold. Payment instruction rejected. VRP consent suspended pending review. Customer notified. Per-payment SCA required to reinstate.

design_decisions.decision: VRP consent authorisation follows the same OAuth 2.0 authorisation code flow as JRN-010 (Open Banking Consent). The consent record is owned by SVC-009 (Domestic Payments, CAP-003) as the payment-capable service, not SVC-017 (Digital Channels).
design_decisions.rationale: VRP is a payment product owned by CAP-003. SVC-017 acts as the API gateway/channel; it does not own payment data. Consistent with Faster Payment (JRN-002) and Open Banking Payment (JRN-010) ownership patterns.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: SVC-017 owning the consent — rejected because it would make CAP-007 a data owner, violating the principle that channels do not own domain entities.

design_decisions.decision: VRP payments do not require per-payment SCA once consent is active. The consent grant itself satisfies the SCA delegation requirement per FCA cVRP framework.
design_decisions.rationale: Core value proposition of VRP vs Direct Debit is elimination of per-payment friction. FCA cVRP framework permits consent-level SCA delegation within defined parameters.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Per-payment SCA for amounts above a threshold — rejected as it replicates the friction VRP is designed to eliminate; instead fraud scoring (SVC-013) provides the risk control.
